Inside a Consilium expert

How much depth a virtual industry expert actually holds — and how that depth turns a CXO question into a grounded answer.

Generated 2026-06-20 · 17 experts live on main · every field machine-gated by gateExpertPack

01The faculty, by the numbers

An expert is not a prompt. It is a structured object of ~80 hand-grade fields. Across the 17 experts on main today that is 1,323 discrete authored fields — each one validated by a deterministic content gate (depth bar, value-mechanism, metric-reference integrity, planning-range benchmarks, hedge rules).

02One expert, thirteen layers

Real content pulled from the Healthcare Revenue Cycle expert. Every other expert carries the same thirteen layers at the same depth.

⚕
Healthcare Revenue Cycle Expert
industry-function · anchored to Epic Resolute PB/HB · excludes payer adjudication + clinical care (separate experts)
Operating metric — 1 of 11 (each carries a benchmark range, data source, and rationale)
Net collection rate — planning range 95–99% · source: 835 remittances vs contractual allowed (Resolute PB/HB)
Why it matters: isolates true yield from contractual write-offs — a 2-point gap on a $2B net-revenue system is ≈ $40M.
Failure mode — 1 of 6
Front-end-seeded denial spiral
Detect: denials concentrated in CARC CO-27 (eligibility) / CO-197 (auth) by access point. Diagnostic: “what share of denials trace to front-end errors, measured back to the originating registrar?”
AI play — 1 of 5 · with control posture + the exact metrics it moves
Denial prediction & prevention  human-in-the-loop
Score claims pre-submission and route high-risk ones to correction before they ship. Moves: initial denial rate, clean claim rate, net collection rate. Risk: the model must explain why a claim is high-risk so staff can act.
Evidence rule — what proof a claim requires
Denial-rate claims require 835 (CARC/RARC) joined to 837, broken out by reason, payer, and access point
Rejects as weak evidence: “a single staff-reported percentage with no remit-level breakdown.”
Hedge rule — confident synthesis, honestly marked
No tenant contract data → “Across provider revenue cycles, denial rates typically run…”
Frames the answer as an industry pattern, not the tenant’s measured number — never refuses, never fabricates a specific figure.
Success model — the CXO stuck-point, answered
P(success): high adoption: high ROI clarity: high
Why high: revenue-cycle outcomes are directly attributable in remit/ledger data, so ROI is unusually firm — the main haircut is payer response eroding recoveries over time, not measurement difficulty.
…and the rest
4 reference architectures (financial-clearance hub, denials-triage workflow, autonomous-coding pipeline, contract-variance engine) · value model + 3 haircut factors · output recipes (denials → cost-stack, AR → line, cash impact → value-bridge) · 5 systems of record · 5 accountable roles · terms of art (DNFB, CARC/RARC, net collection rate, CC/MCC, 835/837).

03How an expert comes to life

The same flow runs for every surface. The expert’s authored content — not the model’s imagination — supplies the numbers, the framing, and the honesty.

CXO asks
“How exposed are we on claim denials, and what would fix it?”
↓
Router (W1.1)
Summons Healthcare Revenue Cycle by industry + keywords; infers output shape → table + value-bridge.
↓
Expert grounds the answer (W1.3)
Pulls its denial metrics (95–99% / 5–10% bands), the front-end-spiral failure mode, the denial-prevention play, and the evidence rule (needs 835+837) — hedging to “industry pattern” where the tenant’s data is thin.
↓
Ava answers · AgentAnswer
“Denials are your biggest controllable leakage. Best-in-class is <5%; ~65% of denials are never reworked, so the initial rate is largely permanent loss. The fix is front-end prevention, not back-end rework.”
▦ table: denials by reason ▟ value-bridge: cash recovered ❝ cites 835/837 odds: high / high / high
